verdict.rationale: PostHog Desktop's coding agents can be given "Other MCP servers for services such as issue trackers, design tools, and internal APIs" alongside PostHog's own MCP server, showing PostHog can consume external MCP tools as a client. However this is documented only briefly for the Desktop app specifically, not as a general platform-wide capability, with no detail on configuration UX, supported server types, or limits, and no independent/hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: broader documentation of MCP-client support across PostHog products (not just Desktop), configuration details/UX for adding third-party servers, and independent verification that it works in practice.
